title: Tagliatelle ai Funghi
subtitle: A rich Italian pasta with chestnut mushrooms and a creamy sauce
excerpt: A classic Italian pasta where mushrooms take centre stage. Chestnut mushrooms are fried hard to concentrate their flavour, then brought together with cream, Parmesan, and a splash of pasta water.
sourceNotes: Northern Italian home-cook tradition; mushroom tagliatelle is a staple across Emilia-Romagna and Piedmont.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The mushroom base can be made a couple of hours ahead. Reheat, add the cream, then toss with freshly cooked pasta.

content.text: Tagliatelle ai funghi is a satisfying pasta that rewards patience with the mushrooms. They need a very hot, dry pan and room to breathe so they brown deeply rather than stewing in their own liquid. The cream sauce comes together in under two minutes once the mushrooms are ready.

items.prepNote: finely grated, plus more to serve

content.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a rolling boil. Start the sauce while you wait.
Heat a wide pan over high heat until very hot. Add the olive oil and the mushrooms in a single layer. Do not stir for 2 minutes. Toss and cook for another 3 minutes until deeply browned.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the butter and the sliced garlic. Stir for one minute until the garlic softens and smells fragrant. Season with salt.
Cook the tagliatelle in the boiling water for 1 minute less than the packet time. Reserve a large mugful of pasta water before draining.
Pour the double cream into the mushroom pan. Stir and let it bubble gently for one minute. Add a splash of pasta water.
Add the drained tagliatelle directly to the pan. Toss over low heat for one minute, adding more pasta water as needed until the sauce coats every strand.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the Parmesan and black pepper. Scatter over the flat parsley. Serve immediately in warmed bowls.

items.symptom: The mushrooms are pale and sitting in liquid.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough, or the mushrooms were crowded.
items.fix: Use the widest pan you have. Do not add oil until the pan is smoking hot. Cook in two batches if needed, and do not touch the mushrooms for the first 2 minutes.

items.symptom: The cream sauce is thin and slides off the pasta.
items.cause: The cream was not reduced, or not enough pasta water was used to emulsify the sauce.
items.fix: Let the cream bubble for a full minute before adding the pasta. Toss vigorously with pasta water to build the emulsion.

items.symptom: The garlic has a bitter, burnt taste.
items.cause: It was added to a pan that was still on high heat.
items.fix: Always turn the heat down to medium before adding the garlic. Sliced garlic burns much faster than whole cloves.
